criterion: The home hero reads as one calm, centred composition with generous space above the group, the gradient product mark, the heading, the lead line and the two controls stacked as a single group.
evaluation_rule: The HOME HERO is the first band at the root address. Yes if the mark, the heading, the lead line and the two controls sit centred in one vertical group with clear space above the mark and no competing element beside them. No if any of the five sits off the centre line, the group is split or pressed against the header, or a second focal element competes with the heading.

criterion: Neighbouring bands on the home surface are told apart by their change of ground alone, with nothing drawn in the seam between two of them.
evaluation_rule: The BANDS are the six home regions from the hero down to the closing band: hero, product rail, consistency console, industry explorer, customer proof and closing band. The header's bottom hairline and the footer's top rule belong to the chrome and are not band seams. Answer yes when every seam between two of those six bands carries no line, border or shadow. Answer no when any of those five seams carries one.

criterion: On the Tessera product route, each claim band states its capability as a specific promise a buyer could challenge, in plain sentences rather than marketing adjectives.
evaluation_rule: A CLAIM BAND is one of the eight bands on the Tessera product route, one per highlight line. Yes if each band's heading and paragraph state a concrete, checkable property of the database, such as what a read returns or what happens during a partition. No if any band's paragraph rests on adjectives such as fast, powerful or seamless without stating a property.

criterion: A product card and the filter bar's controls on the product index each show a finished resting, pointed-at, pressed and focused look.
evaluation_rule: The PRODUCT INDEX is the public card grid under the heading Every product on the platform, with a sticky filter bar holding a name field and two selectors. Yes if a card lifts on a soft shadow when pointed at, a control pointed at takes a pale cool-grey fill, pressed text and pointed-at link text turn a darker blue than the resting action blue, a focused control shows a visible ring, and nothing wears an unstyled or placeholder look. No if any of those four looks is absent or identical to rest, or a placeholder style remains.

criterion: On the datasheet library, every card's cover shows that document's own generated first page, its title set in Manrope, rather than a photograph.
evaluation_rule: The DATASHEET LIBRARY is the public surface at the datasheet address. MANROPE is the display family the product sets its headings in, a rounded geometric face distinct from the Inter body text. Yes if every cover reads as a generated document page whose title is set in Manrope. No if any cover is anything other than a drawn page of that document, or its title is not set in Manrope.

criterion: The industry explorer keeps its six industries listed beside the proof panel on the home surface, the chosen one marked.
evaluation_rule: The INDUSTRY EXPLORER is the two-pane band on the home surface. A WIDE WINDOW is one the width of a laptop screen or wider. Yes if, at that width, the six industries stay listed in one pane while the proof panel sits in the other, with the selected industry visibly marked in the list. No if, at that width, the list and the panel do not sit side by side with the list fully visible and the selected industry marked.

criterion: Under a request for reduced motion, the console route shows a still, labelled diagram of its four parts, each with a one-line caption.
evaluation_rule: The CONSOLE ROUTE is the public surface at the console address. REDUCED MOTION is the setting a visitor turns on to stop animation. Yes if, with reduced motion requested, the region map, the write-then-read strip, the clock readout and the partition control each stand still with a one-line caption beneath. No if any part still slides, rotates, narrows, fills or loops, or any part stands without its caption; a shortened opacity fade does not count as movement.

criterion: On a first visit to the home surface, the cookie choice band leaves the hero's Get started for free and Contact sales controls visible and pressable before any choice is made.
evaluation_rule: The COOKIE CHOICE BAND is the band docked to the foot of the viewport on a first visit, offering Accept and Decline. Yes if, before any choice, both hero controls can be seen whole and pressed. No if the band overlaps either control or dims the page behind a backdrop.

criterion: Selecting a product row on the desk product list leaves the table in view beside the filled detail pane, so a staff member keeps their place in the list.
evaluation_rule: The DESK PRODUCT LIST is the signed-in desk surface with a table of products on the left and a detail pane on the right. A yes needs the table to stay visible beside the filled pane on a laptop-width window, with the selected row still on screen. Otherwise, when the pane replaces or covers the table or the selected row scrolls out of sight, the answer is no.

criterion: Across the public surfaces, one mid, vivid blue marks what a visitor can act on or has selected, and none of the four brand hues fills a button or colours a link's text.
evaluation_rule: A visitor CAN ACT ON a link, a button or a filter control. The FOUR BRAND HUES are a light vivid blue, a mid soft green, a light vivid red and a mid vivid orange. The COMMIT-WAIT BAR is the bar in the console's clock readout that fills while a write waits. A darker step of the action blue counts as the action blue. Yes if the action blue sits only on actionable or selected things and the commit-wait bar, no brand hue fills a button or colours a link's text, and no surface is flooded by one hue family. No if the blue marks any other inert element, a brand hue fills a button or colours a link's text, or one hue family floods a surface.

criterion: On a family page, the family name and the editorial intro stand in the deepest neutral, and the standfirst and each product card's supporting or metadata line read visibly lighter than the intro.
evaluation_rule: A FAMILY PAGE is the public page for one product family, with its name at display size, a one-sentence standfirst and a paragraph of editorial intro. Yes if the name and intro share the darkest text tone and the standfirst and card supporting lines read lighter than the intro. No if the standfirst or a supporting line matches or exceeds the intro's darkness, or the name reads lighter than the intro.

criterion: The failure red or the success green on the contact-sales form marks something that neither refused nor completed, or needed copy is set in the placeholder grey.
evaluation_rule: The FAILURE RED is the hue the form gives a refused field or its failure banner. The SUCCESS GREEN is the hue of the banner that confirms a stored request. The PLACEHOLDER GREY is the light cool neutral of the hint text inside an empty field. Yes if the red marks a field or banner that refused nothing, the green appears before a submission succeeds, or a label or instruction is set in the placeholder grey. No if the red stays on refusals, the green on the success banner and the grey on hints.

criterion: The product rail's one-card advance and a band's fade in from below on the home surface each move briefly and smoothly.
evaluation_rule: The PRODUCT RAIL is the horizontally scrolling row of dark product cards under the heading Products that hold their promises. BRIEFLY AND SMOOTHLY means the movement eases in and out and is over in a moment. Answer yes when both the rail's advance and a band's entrance ease and settle in a moment. Answer no when either jumps, stutters or keeps drifting.

criterion: At a phone width, the Tessera product route still reads comfortably: claim paragraphs keep a readable line length, and the dropdown sub-nav, the hero and the highlights each keep clear space from one another.
evaluation_rule: A PHONE WIDTH is a window the width of a phone held upright. The TESSERA PRODUCT ROUTE is the public page for the flagship database. The HIGHLIGHTS are the card listing the product's eight highlight lines as jump links. The SUB-NAV is the product's section menu, which becomes a dropdown above the content on a narrow window. Yes if, at that width, each claim paragraph wraps to lines a reader can follow without zooming, with space on both sides, and the sub-nav control, the hero and the highlights each keep breathing room from the next. No if claim paragraphs run to the screen edge or break into lines of only a few words, or the sub-nav control, the hero and the highlights sit crowded against one another with no breathing room.
